description:
Experiment: an agent sculpts a sphere by drawing weighted SVG strokes on the /ui/multiview 4x2 grid.

Pipeline:
1. Render a quad-sphere (reasonably dense cage) in MeshNodeViewerScene and capture /ui/multiview. The response gives center, distance and viewOrder; each cell's az/el are the fixed table in MultiviewScreenshot, so every pixel maps back to a camera ray.
2. The agent returns an SVG over the grid: one <polyline data-strength="-1..1"> per stroke (positive = ridge, negative = valley).
3. Lift: map each SVG point to its cell and view, unproject to a ray, intersect the mesh (analytic ray-sphere is fine for iteration 0; a mesh raycast once the shape has moved).
4. Snap the lifted path to a chain of cage edges.
5. Apply the strength. Mode B (build first): displace the stroke's vertices along the normal by strength * scale with a smooth falloff, and crease the chain's edges with |strength|. Mode A (pure crease, mark_edges label="crease" then subdivision_surface): included for comparison; on a sphere it alone only makes faint seams.
6. Subdivide, recapture multiview, feed it back to the agent, and repeat.

Prior art (none does weighted agent strokes): Nealen et al. 2005 sketch-based detail-preserving mesh editing, SilSketch 2007, Kolliopoulos "View Dependent Modeling" (sphere base, view-blended edits), VLM handle-based mesh deformation (arXiv 2506.04562), LL3M (arXiv 2508.08228).

Round 2 of the experiment: goal-driven. The agent sculpts toward a target, a skull: tmp/mesh68/goal/Skull_reference.png in the worktree, a front render of the user's Blender skull sculpt. The .blend is not on this machine; if the user supplies an export, compare multiview against multiview. The agent changes the tools in whatever way gets closest to the goal, starting with the improvements below.

Tool improvements:
- Each round builds on the last: the current sculpted surface is stored, and a new round sculpts on top of it instead of re-evaluating every stroke from the sphere, so later rounds cannot undo earlier ones.
- Overlaps are combined by sign: same-sign strokes take the max magnitude, opposite-sign strokes add.
- Falloff width comes from each polyline's SVG stroke-width (screen pixels converted to surface distance at the lift depth).
- Lifted points are weighted by how face-on the surface is: points where the normal is near-perpendicular to the view ray are down-weighted or dropped.
- Whatever else the skull needs (e.g. a closed <polygon>/<path> region for eye sockets and the nasal cavity, mirror symmetry, a carve/smooth op per stroke), when the goal shows it is needed.
definition-of-done:
1. An automation route (or ixdar-cli command) takes a multiview response plus an SVG of weighted polylines and returns the lifted edge chains with their strengths.
2. Mode B (normal displacement with falloff plus crease) and mode A (crease only) are both applied to a sphere through the node/DSL graph and visible in MeshNodeViewerScene.
3. A demo loop of at least 3 rounds: an agent draws strokes, the sphere is sculpted, multiview is recaptured. The round-by-round multiview PNGs and SVGs are saved under tmp/.
4. A launch.json entry opens the final sculpted sphere scene.
5. Findings (what lifted well, how strokes from different views conflict, mode A vs B) are written into the ticket's changes-made.

6. Rounds build on each other, overlaps combine by sign, stroke-width sets the falloff, and lifted points are weighted by viewing angle.
7. A goal-driven run of several rounds toward the skull reference, with each round's multiview PNG, SVG and lift output saved under tmp/mesh68/skull/.
8. An animation (GIF or MP4 under tmp/mesh68/skull/) that steps through the rounds: for each round, that round's SVG strokes overlaid on the multiview grid before it is applied, then the sculpted result after it. The final frame shows the result next to the goal image.
9. A launch.json entry opens the final skull sculpt.

10. mesh-compare uses the KD-tree path: the route and BatchDslEvaluator both go through KDTree3D, the brute-force loop in computeAllMetrics is gone, and the parsed reference is cached by path, so comparing against the full decimated skull (57k vertices) finishes well inside the CLI's 10 s timeout.
11. Line-art strokes: data-kind="silhouette" polylines drag the current outline in the stroke's view, sideways in screen space, until it meets the stroke. data-kind="ridge"/"valley" are the existing displacement polylines. Filled polygons are kept for cavities only.
12. Further skull rounds that use silhouette strokes, continuing from the round-8 cage, scored against the full goal mesh. The animation is extended with them.
13. A headlight comparison on the skull: curvature multiview of the final sculpt and of the goal, with and without --headlight.
testing-plan:
1. Draw a single horizontal stroke on the Front cell; check it lifts to the sphere's front equator in every other view.
2. Draw a strength +1 stroke and a strength -1 stroke; check the ridge rises and the valley sinks.
3. Draw the same stroke on Front and on 3/4 Front-R; check they land on overlapping edges, and record how the strengths combine.
4. Run the 3-round agent loop and compare the multiview grids.
todos: DONE : Next pass: stroke-driven local refinement. Each stroke's stroke-width and its gap to nearby strokes, converted to surface distance at the lift point, set the edge length needed. Before lifting, subdivide only the faces within the stroke's falloff region until their edges are below that length (about 1/3 of the stroke width), close T-junctions at the boundary with transition triangles, and carry crease marks onto the split edges. Goal: the skull's teeth become sculptable.
unknowns: When strokes from two views hit the same edges, average the strengths or take the max?
Does displacement need a Laplacian/smooth falloff solve, or is a geodesic-distance kernel enough?
changes-made: Built: StrokeLift route (/mesh/stroke-lift, cli stroke-lift); stroke_sculpt node (StrokeSculptNode) over geometry/mesh/data/sculpt/{StrokeSculpt, StrokeChain, EdgeDistances}; MultiviewScreenshot's view table is now the shared VIEW_AZIMUTH_ELEVATION_RADIANS/VIEW_LABELS constants. The quad sphere primitive emits unwelded quads (V=4F), so the DSL welds it with merge_by_distance before sculpting. Round PNGs/SVGs: worktree tmp/mesh68/round0-3.png, round1-3.svg; tests test1-3 there too.

Lift accuracy: a horizontal stroke on the Front cell lifted to y=-0.001, z>0 (front equator, |p|=0.99 on the limit surface). Latitude strokes drawn at y=+-0.45 lifted to 0.447-0.450. No misses inside the silhouette. After round 1 the lift ran on the displaced subdivided mesh (mesh raycast, z up to 1.15), and snapping to the cage's nearest vertices still worked because cage and limit surface stay close. Points near a view's silhouette are the weak spot: the 3/4 Front-R copy of the equator stroke lifted its grazing end to x=-0.41,y=0.045 instead of x=-0.5,y=0.

Cross-view conflicts: the same equator stroke drawn on Front (s=1) and 3/4 Front-R (s=0.5) snapped to 25 shared edges out of 28/26 (26 of 29/27 vertices). Overlap combines by largest magnitude per vertex for displacement and by max for crease, so a stroke repeated from a second view never doubles the bump; the result was indistinguishable from the Front stroke alone. Summing would make the duplicate strokes from different views compound. Opposite-sign overlaps resolve to whichever is larger: in round 2 the eye-socket valleys (-0.9) flattened most of the round-1 brow/nose bulge they overlapped.

Mode A vs B: mode A (crease only, weight 2|s|) on the sphere is close to invisible. Over all three rounds' strokes it changed 5e-5 of the multiview pixels by at most 13/255, as faint seams, because the creased cage edges already lie on the sphere. Mode B gives clear ridges, valleys, a chin, a nose and ears, visible in every view. Its crease shows as a thin sharp line along the stroke inside the soft falloff bump (the nose reads as a creased line).

Sculpting loop (3 rounds, goal a face): round 1 brow+nose+mouth merged into one muzzle with a mouth groove, because the fixed 0.4 falloff is wider than the 0.2 spacing between features. Round 2 sockets+chin carved the muzzle and left the nose as a creased line. Round 3 nose+ears from the Right/Left cells gave a crude face, with ears that read in all 8 views. Main limitation: the agent cannot set width per stroke. A per-stroke falloff (e.g. from SVG stroke-width) is the next lever, and the multiview's dark low-contrast shading makes small features hard for the agent to judge.

Round 2 tools: (1) stroke_sculpt gets base/store ports. Each round loads the cage the previous one stored (SculptCageFile: an OBJ with quads kept and '#crease a b w' lines) and stores its own, so rounds build on each other, and any stored round can be branched from. (2) Overlaps combine by sign: same sign keeps the larger magnitude, opposite signs add. (3) stroke-width sets the falloff radius: SVG pixels times the camera's world-per-pixel at each lifted point (Camera3D.worldPerPixel). (4) Each lifted point is weighted by |n.v|, dropped below 0.25 and full above 0.65, so silhouette points count less; the lift reports a per-stroke 'grazing' count.

Added because the skull needed them: <polygon> fill regions (the interior is sampled at the lift spacing and every sample becomes a source at full strength), for orbits, nasal cavity and big masses. data-mirror="x", for bilateral features drawn once. data-op="smooth" (Laplacian relax weighted by the stroke's kernel), after round 2 crumpled the sides. Automatic anti-fold measures after round 2 showed back-face slivers: normals averaged over the one-ring twice before displacing, and a tangential relax of moved vertices. Also fixed a bug in MeshDistance.computeAllMetrics: it compared squared distances against an unsquared minimum, so it did not return the nearest distance.

Skull run (goal: the user's Skull.obj, decimated by vertex clustering and centred, width 2, under tmp/mesh68/goal/; same 8 views and framing; score: ixdar-cli mesh-compare --normalize against a 7.7k-vertex copy). Chamfer by round 0..8: 0.0494, 0.0401, 0.0299, 0.0284, 0.0271, 0.0262, 0.0267 (rejected), 0.0273 (rejected), 0.0261 (round 8, branched from 5). Hausdorff 0.196 -> 0.122. Overall a 47% chamfer reduction. The side silhouette reads as a skull (vault, undercut skull base, jaw in front), and the orbits and nasal opening read in the 3/4 views. Missing: the zygomatic arches, teeth, the open lower jaw and sharp orbit rims. All data is in tmp/mesh-68-measurements.json and tmp/mesh68/skull/.

Findings: a stroke moves surface along the normals it lands on, which face the camera of the cell it was drawn in. So 'move this down' must be drawn from the Bottom cell, and a Right-cell fill meant to lengthen the jaw grew cheek balls sideways. Gross proportion took 4 rounds, because normal displacement cannot stretch; the start was an ellipsoid placed on the goal's vault. Features finer than the cage (teeth, about 1.5 cage edges) lift to 2 points and do nothing, which needs a refine op or a denser cage. The score caught two bad rounds the eye might have kept (a maxilla fill that became a snout; a 3/4 smooth that blurred the orbits), and base/store made abandoning them a one-flag branch. Crease from chain strokes makes sharp lines that read as cuts on a skull, so the skull used fills and smooth almost exclusively.

mesh-compare: computeAllMetrics now answers each direction's nearest-vertex query with a KDTree3D over the other mesh; the brute O(N*M) loop is gone, so Compare and BatchDslEvaluator (which calls it) both use the tree. Compare caches the parsed reference by path and modified time. Response fields are unchanged. On the 7.7k copy the KD-tree gives the fixed brute-force numbers to float rounding: chamfer 0.026143637 vs 0.026143635, hausdorff 0.12196956 vs 0.12196954. Against the full 57k-vertex goal the brute version hit the CLI's 10 s timeout. Now a cold call takes 0.35 s and a cached call 0.26 s, wall time including the ~0.1 s CLI overhead. From round 9 every round is scored against the full goal, and rounds 0-8 were rescored on it (chamferFull in tmp/mesh-68-measurements.json).

Silhouette strokes: data-kind="silhouette" polylines lift to the view's eye, view axis and one view ray per point. SilhouetteDrag finds the cage's contour vertices for that eye (vertex-normal facing changes sign across an edge). For each one it intersects the stroke's rays with the plane through the vertex perpendicular to the view axis, and drags the vertex in that plane onto the nearest stroke point. Vertices more than the stroke-width reach away, or past the stroke's ends, are left alone. The geodesic falloff spreads each drag into the surface (SilSketch-style). The first try folded the forehead, because neighbours took drags from different contour vertices; blurring the drag field over the one-ring 6 times fixed that, at +0.0004 chamfer. data-kind ridge/valley force the sign of displacement polylines. Polygons are used only for cavities.

Skull rounds 9-11 (line art, from the round-8 cage, curvature shading): outline_diff.py traces goal and sculpt outlines per cell and prints where they part by more than 8 units, with the goal's points along each run; every polyline traces those points. Full-goal chamfer: round 8 0.0253 -> 9 0.0224 (face profile 30 units forward, jaw underside 40 up, jaw sides in, cranium top out) -> 10 0.0178 (vault width and length from Back/Top/Right, occiput down, skull-base gap carved) -> 11 0.0170 (ramus edge, jaw width from Back). Over rounds 0-11 that is 0.0491 -> 0.0170 (-65%). The three silhouette rounds removed 33% of round 8's chamfer, more than rounds 3-8 of fills together. Proportion now matches within ~10 units in every view except the jaw region of the 3/4 views. The features (orbits, nose, teeth, cheekbones) are still round 5's crude fills.

Headlight test (curvature multiview, final sculpt and goal, with and without --headlight; tmp/mesh68/skull/headlight/). Silhouette-rim luminance std, over object pixels within 12 px of the outline: sculpt 27.9 -> 29.8 (+7%), goal 33.8 -> 43.1 (+28%). Mean brightness rises ~13 levels in both. Verdict: it barely changes the sculpt; on the goal it brightens the rims of fine detail. It did not change what the drawing agent can read: the silhouette rounds compared outline masks, which shading does not affect, and the curvature look alone already shows the creases.
review-summary: The stroke sculptor gains line-art silhouette strokes that drag the sculpt's outline onto a traced goal outline, and mesh-compare now runs through a KD-tree with a cached reference. Three silhouette rounds cut the skull's chamfer by a third; F5 'MESH-68: mesh-viewer skull sculpt' opens the result.
